criteria.reasoning: The report calls him "co-founder and former CEO of Netflix" and says he "Founded Netflix in 1997; led it as CEO until 2023." Both the founding year and the end of his CEO tenure are correct.

His only present-tense Netflix title is "Currently Chairman (as of mid-2020s)", which is his correct current title. The report never calls him CEO or Executive Chairman today and lists no current Facebook/Meta or Microsoft board seat.
The report never mentions his April 2026 announcement that he will not stand for re-election to Netflix's board in June 2026.

The report names Netflix equity as his main wealth source and gives sourced figures in range ("~$6.6 billion (Forbes, 2025)", "~$4–6B"). But it describes his stake as "historically ~2% ownership post-donation". The post-January-2024 position is the latest one it states, so it effectively presents his current stake as about 2%, which is barred (it is under 1%).
Patty Quillin's name appears only in the titles of cited links. The report's own text never names her as his wife or co-donor; the $120 million HBCU gift is credited to Hastings alone.

The report lists "Donor-advised fund at Silicon Valley Community Foundation" and "Hastings Fund (education-focused)" as his vehicles, and a "$100 million initial commitment to Hastings education fund". It also routes the 2024 gift to the "Hastings Fund (via Silicon Valley Community Foundation)". No wrong year, amount, sponsor or structure is given.
The report states "$1.1 billion (2024) → Hastings Fund (via Silicon Valley Community Foundation)" and "Donated ~$1.1B in stock in 2024". The value, year and SVCF/DAF recipient all match.

The report says only "$200 million (with partners) → City Fund (charter school expansion)." It never gives the 2018 launch and never names the Arnolds as the anchor partner, so the defining elements of the criterion are missing.

The report states "$120 million (2020) → United Negro College Fund, Morehouse College, Spelman College (HBCU scholarships)." The total, year and three recipients are correct, with no extra or substituted recipient.
The report never mentions the Charter School Growth Fund or his board seat there.
The report never mentions Lone Rock or the Bailey, Colorado educators' retreat.
The capacity section gives "Transformational gift: $50M–$200M" and, for this opportunity, "Likely $10M–$50M+". Both ranges top out above $40 million.

The strategy recommends "Engage through existing networks", including the "Charter school ecosystem (e.g., City Fund connections)", and offers to map "warm intro paths". It recommends no cold letter, Netflix contact or unsolicited application. The "requiring formal proposals" remark does not claim that unsolicited proposals are accepted or that an application process is open.
The report states "historically ~2% ownership post-donation". This contradicts the fact sheet's stake of under 1% (Forbes: less than 1%), and the tolerances allow only "about 1%" or "under 1%".
